A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TPA/T6 research and contain complete corresponding main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–I. Pages 3–46 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v5 reports original language-model training, downstream benchmark results, and decoding-time measurements in Section 6, with additional evaluations and ablations in the appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains the original training results, downstream evaluations, decoding measurements, and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The TPA factorization, T6 architecture, FlashTPA algorithms, and appendix variants are unchanged. The new mentions of output gating and KV shifting assert compatibility without adding a method component or procedure.

E1.justification: FineWeb-Edu training, downstream benchmark coverage, and decoding test scenarios are unchanged. No evaluations using additional positional encodings, output gating, or KV shifting are introduced.

E2.justification: The same MHA, MQA, GQA, and MLA baselines participate in the language-model comparisons. The optimized decoding comparators and comparator membership in appendix experiments are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H retain the same data splits, training budgets, model configurations, zero-shot and two-shot protocols, metrics, and decoding settings.

E4.justification: The higher-order TPA evaluation, non-contextual factor comparisons, rank ablations in Figure 10, and learning-rate analyses in Figure 11 and Tables 17–18 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Run and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged. Checklist item 7 in both versions explicitly states that error bars are omitted because repeated LLM experiments would be computationally expensive.

E6.justification: All numerical results and result plots are unchanged, including TPA’s 51.41% average in Table 2 and TPA-KV only’s 53.52% average in Table 3. No new empirical findings accompany the compatibility assertions.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1 and C.1, their Appendix D proofs, and the other mathematical derivations are unchanged. The broader introductory compatibility assertion is not accompanied by a new formal statement or proof.

C1.justification: Section 1 broadens compatibility from RoPE to "any possible position encodings"; contribution 3 additionally names "output gate and KV shifting." This extends the compatibility contribution while retaining the principal TPA/T6 efficiency and performance claims, abstract, and conclusion.

C2.justification: The introduction expands the stated applicability to arbitrary positional encodings and additional attention modifications. Existing result interpretations, mechanism explanations, and Appendix I’s limitation concerning generalization to other modalities remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Initialization, kernel pseudocode, hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and code/data access links are unchanged. No implementation guidance is added for the newly asserted integrations.

R1.justification: The references and Appendix E’s related-work positioning are unchanged. Qwen is added to contribution 3’s examples, but it was already named and cited in v5’s preceding compatibility paragraph.

P1.justification: Two introductory passages receive localized wording changes, the compatibility paragraph is merged into the preceding paragraph, and the version/date stamp is updated. The section organization and remaining text are unchanged.

P2.justification: Page 2 has localized text reflow and tighter spacing around Figure 1’s caption. The figure graphic and caption wording remain unchanged, as do all other figures and tables.

improvement.justification: v6 presents compatibility with arbitrary positional encodings, output gating, and KV shifting as demonstrated, while Section 3.2 and Appendices C–D retain RoPE-specific compatibility results and the experiments remain unchanged. The PDFs provide no accompanying explanation or demonstration of the broader integrations. This modestly weakens claim precision and evidential support without changing the underlying method or empirical results.
